essentials.title: Walk through every classroom and keep a short log
essentials.description: Short, regular walkthroughs keep you close to teaching and learning. Note what you see and give brief feedback; walkthroughs are developmental and do not count towards a teacher's F2 score.

source.quote: Weekly walkthroughs by the principal occur in every classroom and are documented.

essentials.title: Lead your weekly leadership team meeting
essentials.description: Use it to plan and coordinate the week's activities. Short daily huddles are also part of the normal Principal Operating Cadence.

source.quote: Hold a regular leadership team meeting each week to plan and coordinate the week's activities.

essentials.title: Be visible at the gate and around the school
essentials.description: Greet students in the morning, be there at dismissal, and take short informal walkabouts to connect with students and staff.

source.quote: Greet students at the school gate in the morning and be present during dismissal.

essentials.title: Keep your normal leadership records up to date
essentials.description: Meeting notes, your walkthrough log and budget reviews are your evidence. Record them as you work; evidence must be real and dated, never created or back-filled only for appraisal.

source.quote: Keep normal school leadership records; do not create evidence only for appraisal.

essentials.title: Close the week: safeguarding check and next priorities
essentials.description: Check that any safeguarding concern raised this week was logged and escalated correctly. Then note what you learned this week and your 2–3 "must-win" priorities for next week.

source.quote: As part of the weekly reflection, check whether any safeguarding concerns arose this week and confirm they were logged and escalated correctly.

tasks.title: Lead the HoD coordination meeting
tasks.description: Meet your Heads of Department to coordinate teaching, curriculum and student support. Keep minutes, and track and follow up the action items.
tasks.timing_text: Every two weeks (biweekly) — tick it in the weeks you meet

source.quote: HoD coordination meetings led by the principal are held biweekly. Action items from meetings are tracked and followed up.

tasks.title: Review the school budget (RKAS) for the month
tasks.description: Monthly budget reviews are part of your Operating Cadence. Check spending against the annual budget and plan, and act early on any gap.
tasks.timing_text: Once a month

source.quote: daily huddles, weekly walkthroughs, monthly budget (RKAS) reviews, termly self-evaluation (EDS) cycles, annual vision-and-mission reviews

tasks.title: Hold your monthly 15-minute induction review
tasks.description: Use the one-page status view from the Induction Control Centre: Green / Amber / Red counts, any teacher without a valid mentor, mentors at capacity, overdue observations and checkpoints due soon. End with named actions and dates. Check the system, not private mentoring notes.
tasks.timing_text: Once a month, while any teacher is in induction

source.quote: make sure that the programme is correctly staffed, protected in the timetable, completed on time, quality-checked and escalated when it is not working

tasks.title: Check this month's professional development plan
tasks.description: Make sure this month's PD or in-house training has facilitators, materials and a participant list ready. When network training such as the DTP runs, organise teacher participation and track attendance.
tasks.timing_text: Once a month

source.quote: Review and finalize this month's professional development (PD) plan / in-house training; confirm that facilitators, materials, and participant lists are ready.

tasks.title: Look at observation and walkthrough data
tasks.description: Find the teachers who need support, and spot school-wide teaching patterns that should shape your PD priorities.
tasks.timing_text: Suggested: once a month (the checklist says "regularly")

source.quote: Analyze classroom observation data and walkthrough data regularly to identify teachers who need support.

tasks.title: Review curriculum coverage for the month
tasks.description: With your Academic Coordinator, check that Cambridge syllabus coverage is on schedule. A subject marked "At Risk" needs a documented recovery action; required content is never silently dropped.
tasks.timing_text: Once a month

source.quote: confirm that curriculum teaching is progressing as scheduled, both at a regular (e.g., weekly) pace and in a fuller monthly review

tasks.title: Send the monthly newsletter to parents
tasks.description: Keep parents informed about school activities and student achievements through your usual channels.
tasks.timing_text: Once a month

source.quote: Publish a monthly school newsletter to keep parents informed of activities and achievements.

tasks.title: Refresh safeguarding for the new year
tasks.description: Review the Child Protection Policy, refresh DSL training, brief all staff and update records (Academic Standards Section 9). Confirm the DSL is named and known to all staff, and that all staff, including non-teaching staff, complete their annual safeguarding training.
tasks.timing_text: Start of the academic year

source.quote: Review the Child Protection Policy, refresh DSL training, brief all staff, and update records in accordance with Academic Standards Section 9

tasks.title: Give every new teacher a certified mentor and a welcome
tasks.description: Before a new teacher starts, assign a colleague and an eligible, certified, subject-matched mentor (hard cap: three mentees), protect the timetable reduction and check the safeguarding gate. Welcome each new teacher personally. Ask Eduversal early for a cross-school mentor if you have a gap.
tasks.timing_text: Before the year starts, and whenever a new teacher joins

source.quote: No new teacher is left without a valid named mentor because the school is busy.

tasks.title: Finalise the semester timetable and duty assignments
tasks.description: Confirm teacher assignments, classrooms and duties. At the start of the year, also issue the SK Pembagian Tugas and collect signed receipts, so every staff member knows their teaching load and roles.
tasks.timing_text: Start of each semester

source.quote: Review and finalize the semester timetable, including teacher assignments, classroom placements, and duty responsibilities.

tasks.title: Confirm the school calendar for the year
tasks.description: Include the network dates: EASE Weeks, report distributions and your school's appraisal visit windows. Check external dates against current official sources before you publish them.
tasks.timing_text: Start of the academic year

source.quote: Finalize the school calendar (key dates: holidays, assessments, parent-teacher conferences, etc.).

tasks.title: Tell teachers the appraisal standards and agree objectives
tasks.description: At the start of the appraisal period, make sure every teacher knows the standards they will be appraised against and has objectives for the year. Confirm which appraisal visits (School, Subject Specialist, Teacher) fall in this semester.
tasks.timing_text: Start of the academic year

source.quote: Inform the teacher of the standards against which the teacher’s performance in that appraisal period will be assessed

tasks.title: Check your team understands the EASE Schedule
tasks.description: Confirm your Academic Coordinator and coordinators know the EASE Schedule 26-27 and the school's calendar slots. Keep the three EASE programmes (Growth, Assessment, Academic) separate in purpose, communication and score use.
tasks.timing_text: Start of the academic year

source.quote: confirm that the Academic Coordinator and relevant coordinators understand the current EASE Schedule 26-27

tasks.title: Do a full campus safety review
tasks.description: At the start of each semester, walk the whole campus for safety and cleanliness (a brief check each week is enough in between). Check the fire and earthquake drill schedule, the evacuation plan and first-aid certificates.
tasks.timing_text: Start of each semester

source.quote: Conduct a campus walkthrough to check facility safety and cleanliness — a brief weekly version and a more thorough review

tasks.title: Brief students on safeguarding
tasks.description: Make sure every student knows who to report a concern to, and how.
tasks.timing_text: Start of each semester

source.quote: Include a Safeguarding Awareness briefing for students at the start of each semester — who to report concerns to, and how.

tasks.title: Audit the school WiFi filters
tasks.description: Use the School Network Audit tool. Between audits, review the WiFi and network security logs and content-filtering alerts regularly.
tasks.timing_text: Start and middle of each semester

source.quote: Carry out a full compliance check against PP 17/2025, Permenkomdigi 9/2026, and SE 18/2026.

tasks.title: Plan this semester's formal observation cycle
tasks.description: Every teacher in the appraisal population needs at least three formal observations this semester from the school's own appraisers, recorded in Edunav. Agree who observes whom and take your share. Teachers still in induction are not on this schedule.
tasks.timing_text: Start of each semester

source.quote: formally observes you at least three times per semester — a minimum of six formal observations per academic year

tasks.title: Check every teacher's formal observations are recorded
tasks.description: Before the semester closes, confirm each teacher has at least three formal observations in Edunav Appraisal, with feedback conversations held. Eduversal Subject Specialist observations do not count here; they are formative only.
tasks.timing_text: A few weeks before each semester ends

source.quote: Formal observations are conducted at least 3 times per semester per teacher by the school's own appraiser team

tasks.title: Set up Digital Citizenship & AI roles
tasks.description: Work through the Principal launch checklist: appoint a Digital Citizenship Coordinator and an AI Integration Coordinator (one person may hold both), confirm the safeguarding, privacy and IT leads, and approve the school's Approved AI Tools List.
tasks.timing_text: Start of the academic year

source.quote: Appoint an AI Integration Coordinator, or formally assign both responsibilities to one suitable person.

tasks.title: Name your Portfolio Coordinator and set SLC dates
tasks.description: Assign one Portfolio Coordinator from existing academic leadership. Plan two portfolio-led review / Student-Led Conference cycles, one in each semester, normally in existing parent or reporting windows.
tasks.timing_text: Start of the academic year

source.quote: Each school assigns one coordinator, normally the Academic Coordinator, Cambridge Coordinator, Principal, or another designated senior academic leader.

tasks.title: Check your Cambridge centre basics
tasks.description: Confirm the school's Cambridge International School status, that Cambridge policies are current, that every teacher has a Cambridge Support Hub account, and that Cambridge resources are available to teachers and students.
tasks.timing_text: Suggested: early in the year

source.quote: Make sure all Cambridge-related policies and procedures are up to date.

tasks.title: Check staff data privacy under UU PDP
tasks.description: Confirm that staff data in Edunav is processed correctly with the required consents, and that the Edunav Data Privacy Notice is visible at school and names its sub-processors.
tasks.timing_text: Suggested: once a year, early in the year

source.quote: Confirm that staff data in Edunav is being processed correctly under UU PDP No. 27/2022, and that the required consents have been obtained.

tasks.title: Align school goals with Eduversal's vision and mission
tasks.description: The annual vision-and-mission review is part of your Operating Cadence. Align the school's annual goals with Eduversal's, and update your own vision and mission statements alongside the SOPs where needed.
tasks.timing_text: Once a year, early in the year

source.quote: Review and internalize Eduversal Indonesia's vision, mission, and annual goals, and align the school's own annual goals with them.

tasks.title: Approve the Cambridge exam entries
tasks.description: As Head of Centre, you approve the entry submission your Exams Officer prepares. Check that students' subject combinations were approved and that names match passports or ID.
tasks.timing_text: Before each entry deadline — entries close about 8–10 weeks before the exams; confirm the exact date with your Exams Officer

source.quote: Holds overall accountability for Cambridge compliance. Approves entries, signs the Cambridge Center Annual Declaration

tasks.title: Stay ready to act during each Cambridge exam series
tasks.description: Your Exams Officer runs the exam days; you stay on call. Suspected malpractice must be reported to Cambridge the same day (or by 12:00 the next working day). Check invigilators have had the required safeguarding checks.
tasks.timing_text: Start of each series: Oct/Nov (late September – mid-November) and May/June (late April – early June)

source.quote: The Head of Centre must report all suspected malpractice to Cambridge on the same day

tasks.title: Sign off Cambridge results and lead the analysis
tasks.description: With your Exams Officer, release results securely, then compare them with predicted grades and previous years. Share the analysis with the Academic Board and feed the findings into your School Development Plan.
tasks.timing_text: When results arrive: May/June results early-to-mid August; Oct/Nov results mid-January

source.quote: After each exam series, analyze Cambridge results against predicted grades and prior-year performance, and share the analysis with the Academic Board.

tasks.title: Present the Annual Examinations Report
tasks.description: Each November the Board receives an Annual Examinations Report on participation, outcomes, compliance, incidents and budget. Your Exams Officer supplies the data and you present it. After the Oct/Nov series, also review the examinations policy with your Exams Officer and Quality Nominee.
tasks.timing_text: Each November

source.quote: You supply the data; the Principal presents it.

tasks.title: Sign the Cambridge Centre Annual Declaration
tasks.description: Your Exams Officer prepares it; you sign it. Also check that the school's annual Cambridge School Self-Evaluation (SSE) and registration renewal are on track.
tasks.timing_text: Typically by March

source.quote: The signed Cambridge Centre Annual Declaration — you prepare it, the Principal signs it, typically by March

tasks.title: Submit your Self-Evaluation before each on-site visit
tasks.description: With your Academic Coordinator, complete or update the Self-Evaluation Summary and evidence links in the Evidence Guide workbook for all five domains. Without it the visit is rescheduled. The online Phase 0 Kickoff, about three weeks before Phase 1, launches this work.
tasks.timing_text: At least 5 working days before your school's Phase 1 visit (5 Aug – 18 Sep 2026) and Phase 3 visit (7 Oct – 20 Nov 2026)

source.quote: Before each on-site visit, your school must submit a Self-Evaluation Report covering all five domains.

tasks.title: Prepare your School Programs presentation for Phase 1
tasks.description: A short presentation of programme goals, achievements and challenges (Olympiad, STEAM, extracurricular), linked to your mission and the five domains. Send it to your Visit I Supervisor 3 working days before the visit.
tasks.timing_text: Before your school's Phase 1 visit (5 Aug – 18 Sep 2026)

source.quote: prepare a brief presentation (e.g., slides or documents) summarizing program goals, achievements, and challenges

tasks.title: Get the school ready for the visit team
tasks.description: Confirm the timetable for Specialist observations (with any temporary adjustments), the staff and students for meetings, the workroom, three meeting rooms, catering and a school contact person. Share the Pre-Observation Information with all teachers. You may delegate the arrangements.
tasks.timing_text: 3 working days before each on-site visit (Phase 1 and Phase 3)

source.quote: Confirm the school timetable for formative Specialist lesson observations.

tasks.title: Prepare for the Phase 2 Progress Check-in
tasks.description: Have short updates on the actions agreed at Phase 1 and on D1–D5 progress, and be ready to agree the next actions, owners and deadlines. It is a progress review, not a re-scoring.
tasks.timing_text: Between your Phase 1 and Phase 3 visits; completed by 18 October 2026

source.quote: Prepare brief updates and evidence for previous agreed actions and D1–D5 progress, plus any current challenges or support needed.

tasks.title: Put the two priorities into your School Development Plan
tasks.description: Read the Annual School Quality Report with your leadership team: it gives a Development Rating for each domain, never one overall score. With your Academic Coordinator, carry the two School Development Priorities into the plan. If you disagree with a rating, you may appeal in writing to the CAO within 10 working days.
tasks.timing_text: Within two weeks of receiving your Annual School Quality Report (it arrives within three weeks of your Phase 3 visit)

source.quote: Within two weeks of receiving the report, the school transfers the two School Development Priorities into its School Development Plan.

tasks.title: Write an action plan for each School Development Priority
tasks.description: Work with the Head of Department or lead closest to each priority. Keep it short: two or three actions, one owner, and the evidence that will show change.
tasks.timing_text: Start of Semester II

source.quote: Action plan written for each School Development Priority: desired outcome, two or three actions, an owner, a timeline, and success evidence

tasks.title: Check progress on your two School Development Priorities
tasks.description: Use the priority plan and tracking sheet. Look for early changes in evidence, not only activity.
tasks.timing_text: Mid-Semester II

source.quote: Progress check — are the priority actions running, and is early evidence beginning to change?

tasks.title: Prepare for the Phase 4 Impact Review
tasks.description: For each priority, gather only the evidence linked to it: what was done, what changed, what still needs work and what carries forward. Phase 4 creates no new Domain Rating and needs no large evidence pack.
tasks.timing_text: Before the online Phase 4 Impact Review (May–Jun 2027)

source.quote: The school reviews its two School Development Priorities, what was implemented, what changed, the evidence of impact, what still needs work

tasks.title: Prepare for your leadership observation visit (F2)
tasks.description: For principals in the Principal Appraisal cycle (Year 2 onwards). Know the P1–P8 areas and keep normal evidence easy to reach; do not prepare a special performance. Before the first visit, check you have your written launch confirmation and resolve any questions about level or evidence window.
tasks.timing_text: Observation windows: Sep–Oct 2026 and Feb–Apr 2027

source.quote: Have normal leadership evidence accessible: strategic plans, curriculum/learning review records, operational records, data-review evidence

tasks.title: Complete your F5 self-assessment
tasks.description: For principals in the Principal Appraisal cycle. Name specific evidence, say what changed and name a real development area. A missing F5 leaves the appraisal incomplete.
tasks.timing_text: Twice a year: Semester I / mid-year and late in the year — follow the dates in your launch confirmation

source.quote: Complete both termly self-assessments and an annual reflection.

tasks.title: Encourage honest 360 feedback
tasks.description: For principals in the Principal Appraisal cycle. Staff, parent representatives and student-council representatives respond anonymously. The mid-year cycle is formative only; the late-year cycle is the official F3 evidence.
tasks.timing_text: When each 360 cycle opens: mid-year and late in the year

source.quote: Encourage honest 360 participation without trying to influence responses.

tasks.title: Prepare for your year-end appraisal conversation
tasks.description: For principals in the Principal Appraisal cycle. Know your EASE, Cambridge and Rapor Pendidikan patterns, finish an evidence-based annual reflection, and come with two or three next-year goals you believe in.
tasks.timing_text: Late in the year, before the year-end conversation

source.quote: Know the main outcome patterns in your school before the year-end conversation.

tasks.title: Run the EASE pre-window check
tasks.description: Can you answer yes? Which EASE system is running, which grades and teachers, date confirmed, owners clear, devices, internet, rooms and supervision ready, staff know how scores are used and the confidentiality rules, escalation route known. EASE Growth runs inside normal lessons; in Synchronized Test weeks lessons stop.
tasks.timing_text: Before each EASE window: Week 1 (28 Sep 2026), Week 2 (7 Dec 2026), Grades 4–6 Growth (18–22 Jan 2027), Week 3 (29 Mar 2027), Week 4 (10 May 2027)

source.quote: Before each EASE window, the Principal should be able to answer yes to these questions:

tasks.title: Give teachers notice of EASE Academic
tasks.description: Make sure eligible teachers get the preparation information in good time. Remind everyone that EASE Academic is for professional development only: individual scores go to the teacher alone, and you receive only school-level trends.
tasks.timing_text: Suggested: a few weeks before each EASE Academic date (5 Dec 2026, 15 May 2027)

source.quote: Confirm the list of eligible teachers and the current EASE Academic window in EASE Schedule 26-27.

tasks.title: Review EASE Growth results with your Academic Coordinator
tasks.description: Use the School Baseline Summary to find broad reasoning and literacy support needs. 2026-27 is Version 1: a baseline, not a growth score. Never use Growth results in School Appraisal or individual Teacher Appraisal.
tasks.timing_text: When Eduversal releases the School Baseline Summary after each Growth window (suggested placement)

source.quote: Review approved school-level Growth patterns with the Academic Coordinator when reports are released.

tasks.title: Review EASE Assessment patterns with your Academic Coordinator
tasks.description: Check that scores are in the gradebook, the moderation sample is done where marking is manual, and students below mastery get reteaching and one targeted reassessment within 10 working days. Never treat a single result as a judgement of a teacher.
tasks.timing_text: Suggested: mid-semester, and after the Semester I Synchronized Test results

source.quote: Review school, class, and subject patterns with the Academic Coordinator and decide what support is needed.

tasks.title: Take part in the Assessment Committee
tasks.description: Your Academic Coordinator chairs it and you are a member. It reviews assessment data and student outcomes and plans assessment PD.
tasks.timing_text: Quarterly: August, November and February (the June review falls after the teaching weeks)

source.quote: comprises the School Principal, all Heads of Department (HoDs), and the Learning Support Coordinator where applicable

tasks.title: Run the curriculum implementation checklist
tasks.description: With your Academic Coordinator, check that required Cambridge and national time is protected, every subject has a current Scheme of Work and coverage tracker, and assessment dates avoid overload. Review it again at mid-semester.
tasks.timing_text: Start of each semester; review at mid-semester

source.quote: Use once at the start of each semester and review at mid-semester.

tasks.title: Lead the Stage 4 and Stage 5 induction checkpoints
tasks.description: Observe one full lesson with the induction rubric (not the F2 form) and give Glow / Grow / Go feedback. At Stage 5, sign the final outcome: completed, extended or withdrew. Nothing from induction moves into appraisal.
tasks.timing_text: Stage 5 at the end of a teacher's third induction semester; Stage 4 at the end of Semester 2 (observed lesson by 7 May 2027)

source.quote: Leads the Stage 4 Integration Checkpoint and Stage 5 Final Completion Review.

tasks.title: Review the induction system for the semester
tasks.description: Look at completion of required activities, mentor-capacity gaps, subjects needing cross-school support and common new-teacher needs. Review the system, not individual teachers.
tasks.timing_text: Near the end of each semester

source.quote: At the end of each semester, leadership reviews the system, not teacher rankings.

tasks.title: Close the semester
tasks.description: Check report cards are ready for distribution (Finalterm reports: 19 Dec 2026 and 29 May 2027), review assessment results with your Academic Coordinator, and start planning the next semester.
tasks.timing_text: Last two weeks of each semester

source.quote: Report cards, EASE/Common Assessment result analysis, preliminary planning for the next semester.

tasks.title: Reflect on the semester and adjust your plan
tasks.description: This is your termly self-evaluation (EDS) cycle. Check progress against the school improvement plan and set the priorities for next semester.
tasks.timing_text: End of each semester

source.quote: At the end of each term/semester, reflect on progress against the school improvement plan and adjust priorities for the next term.

tasks.title: Make sure every teacher's End-of-Year Conference is held
tasks.description: The conference scores F3 and finalises each teacher's appraisal record; teachers then receive their report in Edunav. Complete end-of-year performance summaries linked to the results.
tasks.timing_text: Later in Semester II

source.quote: The End-of-Year Conference session, held later in Semester 2, retrieves the accumulated appraisal record

tasks.title: Plan next year's staffing
tasks.description: Review contract renewals and your succession plan for key roles. Make sure safer-recruitment checks (background and references) are complete before any new hire starts.
tasks.timing_text: Semester II (the recruitment cycle typically runs in the second half of the year)

source.quote: Plan vacancies, with priority on Cambridge-qualified subject specialists; coordinate interviews and contract offers.

tasks.title: Prepare next year's budget and RKAS
tasks.description: Draft the annual budget and capital expenditure priorities in line with Eduversal's planning cycle.
tasks.timing_text: Suggested: Semester II, before the new academic / fiscal year

source.quote: Lead or contribute to the school's Annual Work Plan and Budget (RKAS), in line with Eduversal's planning cycle.

tasks.title: Review admissions and re-enrolment
tasks.description: Look at application numbers, the marketing plan, open-house and school-tour dates, and re-enrolment of current students.
tasks.timing_text: Suggested: once a semester (timing varies by school)

source.quote: Review the admissions/enrollment cycle — application numbers, marketing plan, and open house/school tour scheduling.

tasks.title: Check the school website against the standards
tasks.description: Make sure the Academic Section is current.
tasks.timing_text: Suggested: once a semester

source.quote: Check the school website against Website Minimum Standards 26-27; use Website Quality Audit Checklist 26-27 for the formal review

tasks.title: Submit the school's annual report to Eduversal
tasks.description: Send it to the Head of Education at Eduversal Indonesia.
tasks.timing_text: Suggested: end of the year

source.quote: Prepare and submit the school's annual report to the Head of Education at Eduversal Indonesia.

tasks.title: Prepare the handover file for next year
tasks.description: Collect key documents and a summary of achievements and challenges. Make sure textbooks and resources are collected and inventoried, and classrooms cleared.
tasks.timing_text: Near the end of the year

source.quote: Prepare a handover file for the next academic year, including key documents and a summary of achievements and challenges.

tasks.title: Check coursework and moderation deadlines are tracked
tasks.description: Subjects with Cambridge coursework or school-based assessment have internal moderation and submission deadlines. Check that someone is tracking them before each series.
tasks.timing_text: Start of each semester

source.quote: Track internal moderation and submission deadlines for subjects with Cambridge coursework or school-based assessment components.

notes_for_reviewer: Priority: the School Principals Checklist calls itself a running reference ('use it as a running reference'), so tasks taken only from it are marked 'recommended'. Tasks are 'core' where another live document requires the duty of the principal (Teacher / School / Principal Appraisal handbooks, EASE Principal's Guide, Induction Oversight Guide, Exams Officer Handbook, Assessment Policy, DC&AI Implementation Toolkit, Student Learning Overview). Exceptions to check: SP2-013 safeguarding refresh is 'core' (the sibling checklist item calls the staff training 'mandatory'); SP2-028 vision/mission and SP2-055 semester reflection are 'core' because the Principal Appraisal Handbook lists 'annual vision-and-mission reviews' and 'termly self-evaluation (EDS) cycles' in the Operating Cadence, though their quotes come from the checklist. SP2-021 WiFi audit (PP 17/2025, Permenkomdigi 9/2026, SE 18/2026) is left 'recommended'; consider promoting it.

Calendar conflict: calendar-2026-27.txt gives EASE Growth Primary (Grades 4–6) as 17–21 Jan 2027 (17 Jan is a Sunday); the live School Principals Checklist says 18–22 January 2027. Used 18 Jan 2027 (live document wins).

Calendar note: calendar-2026-27.txt treats EASE Week 1 (28 Sep – 2 Oct 2026) and Week 3 (29 Mar – 2 Apr 2027) as skipped, non-teaching weeks, while the live Checklist and EASE Principal's Guide say EASE Growth runs inside the normal class schedule and does not cancel lessons. No task depends on those weeks, but the seeder calendar and the live wording disagree.

SP2-006 HoD coordination meeting: the School Appraisal Handbook (Domain 2, Aspect B) expects principal-led HoD meetings 'biweekly'. The 'when' schema has no biweekly type, so it is 'weekly' with timing_text 'Every two weeks'. Switch if the seeder gains a biweekly type.

SP2-021 WiFi audit uses explicit dates (20 Jul, 14 Sep 2026, 11 Jan, 8 Mar 2027) because one task cannot combine semester_start and semester_mid. The start-of-semester dates are the second teaching week, to spread the opening-week load.

Placements where the live source gives no exact date (said so in timing_text): SP2-029 entry approval (20 Jul 2026, 15 Feb 2027; the Exams Officer Handbook only says entries close about 8–10 weeks before the exams and that Oct/Nov entries are closed by September); SP2-043/044 F5 and 360 (16 Nov 2026, 12 Apr 2027; the Principal Guide says 'Semester I / mid-year' and 'Late-year'); SP2-048 EASE Growth results (19 Oct 2026, 19 Apr 2027; release dates are not in the live docs); SP2-049 EASE Assessment review; SP2-058 next-year RKAS; SP2-059 admissions; SP2-060 website; SP2-061 annual report.

SP2-046 EASE pre-window check uses lead_weeks 1 on dates that mostly fall in skipped weeks. If the seeder falls back to the previous teaching week and then applies the lead, the check shows two teaching weeks before EASE Weeks 1–4 and one week before the Grades 4–6 window. Please confirm. SP2-047 (EASE Academic notice, lead_weeks 3) depends on the same behaviour.

Phase 4 Impact Review is 'May–Jun 2027' in the Quick Reference, Visit Preparation Guide and School Appraisal Handbook, i.e. after the last teaching week (7 May). SP2-041 is therefore a preparation task in the week of 26 Apr 2027.

Annual School Quality Report: the School Appraisal Handbook says every school receives it 'by mid-December 2026'. SP2-038 (transfer the two priorities into the SDP within two weeks) sits in the last Semester I teaching week (30 Nov); schools whose report arrives later will do it over the break or in the first week of Semester II, where SP2-039 (action plans) sits.
Assessment Committee (Assessment Policy §14.3): the fourth meeting is June 2027, after the teaching weeks, so SP2-050 covers August, November and February only.

SP2-032 Annual Examinations Report: the Exams Officer Handbook says 'the Board' receives it each November and the Principal presents it, without saying which board. The task keeps 'the Board'; please confirm the intended body.

Live-document wording to check (not repeated here): Principal Appraisal: Principal Guide 26-27 §10 says 'The Foundation Representative / yayasan receives only…', which equates the FR/GM with the yayasan. The Principal Guide's own word 'composite' (the appraisal composite for the principal) is not used in any task.

Principal Appraisal tasks SP2-042 to SP2-045 apply only from Year 2; Year-1 principals are in protected Principal Induction (Principal Guide §1). Each description says so. A Year-1 Principal Induction overlay (mentor calls etc., Induction Module: Principal 26-27) is not included; the v1 file had one. Decide whether v2 needs a separate overlay.

Checklist items deliberately NOT made principal tasks because the live documents give them to another role: Cambridge entry logistics, venue preparation, invigilation, malpractice briefing and post-series analysis (Checklist Periodic Tasks: 'The Exams Officer coordinates…'); access-arrangement applications, exam-centre documentation and secure storage (Exams Officer Handbook); EASE Assessment calendar planning with subject coordinators, the moderation sample, cross-school moderation, Digital Citizenship curriculum embedding and syllabus-update circulars (Academic Coordinator, per EASE Principal's Guide §6 and Governance & Decision Rights). The principal keeps light oversight through SP2-029/030/031/033, SP2-046/049 and SP2-011.

Other checklist items left out to keep the load light (no timing, very small, or folded into another task's description): ECAs started, learning-support and counsellor meetings, parent office hours, birthdays and celebrations, weekly staff bulletin and Friday 'win' message, monthly attendance/leave reports, vendor contracts, licence renewals, CCTV/visitor management, SOP/handbook validation, EDUNAV readiness and eForm audit, organisational chart, exit interviews, Cambridge PD hours, predicted-grade review. They can be added as extra 'recommended' tasks if fuller coverage is wanted.

Load (by my simulation of the 'when' rules, 36 teaching weeks): every week has 1–8 dated/recurring tasks plus the 5 essentials. The busiest weeks are 27–31 Jul 2026, 1–5 Mar 2027, 26–30 Apr 2027 and 3–7 May 2027 (8 each); 3–7 May is the only May teaching week, so both the 'first' and 'last' monthly tasks land there.
